pll1d3c4-d1e3476.summary: Draws the conclusion from the preceding consideration: we believe the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one God, creator and ruler of every creature, none of them being another, but a Trinity of persons related to one another.
claims: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one God, creator and ruler.
The persons are distinct and mutually related.

pll1d3c4-d1e3495.summary: With the De fide ad Petrum, holds one nature but not one person: one person would deny a true Trinity, and diversity of natures would deny one God. The Father alone begets the one Son, the Son alone is born, the Spirit alone proceeds from Father and Son. No single person could do all three, since, per Augustine, nothing begets itself.
claims: There is one nature of Father, Son, and Spirit, not one person.
Diversity of natures among the persons would destroy the unity of God.
The Father alone begets, the Son alone is born, the Spirit alone proceeds from Father and Son.

pl-l1d3c4.summary: Draws the conclusion of the consideration of the image: with Augustine, we believe that Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one God, creator and ruler, and none is the other, a Trinity of persons related to one another. With the De fide ad Petrum, one essence but not one person: if there were one person the Trinity would not be true, and if natures differed as persons do the Trinity would not be one God. The Father alone begets, the Son alone is born, the Spirit alone proceeds from both; no single person could do all this, since nothing begets itself.
claims: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one God, creator and ruler of all creatures.
The persons are a Trinity of persons related to one another.
There is one nature but not one person.
If the persons differed in nature as they do in property, they would not be one God.
The Father alone begets, the Son alone is born, the Spirit alone proceeds from Father and Son.
